page: Microsoft Azure D48_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2673 v4 processor. This CPU provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs via hyperthreading, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and is bundled with 1229 GB of local storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance dichotomy between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is limited, with both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics falling into the bottom 10% tier. Text processing performance is also weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Conversely, multi-core capabilities are more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all registering in the middle 50% average tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with PassMark memory and database operations, consistently perform within the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the D48_v3 is its low single-threaded execution speed, which impacts tasks like single-threaded compression or text processing. However, its 48 vCPUs and 192 GB RAM provide sufficient resource density for multi-threaded workloads. Large-block memory write speeds and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both sit in the average tier. For LLM inference, prompt processing for small and medium models is average, but text generation speeds are poor. This server is suited for general-purpose multi-threaded workloads, database operations, static web serving, and software compilation, where parallel processing can offset the lower single-core clock speed.
